display.title: Rosh Chodesh: Why the First Day Is the Head of the Month
display.summary_short: On Erev Rosh Chodesh Av, Uncle Yossi explains why the first day of the month is called its 'head', and why our conduct on Rosh Chodesh matters for the whole month.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given on Erev Rosh Chodesh Av. Uncle Yossi points out that the word Rosh in Rosh Chodesh does not mean 'new' but 'head'. Our Sages explain that just as the head guides the whole body and every limb draws its life from it, the first day of the month is the head of all the days that follow. On Rosh Chodesh Hashem grants the blessings for health, life and livelihood, including food, clothing and shelter, for the entire month, and they are then shared out among its days. That is why there are special prayers on Rosh Chodesh, and why we should take extra care with how we behave on that day, when we pass before Hashem, our merciful King, to be judged for good and for blessing.
display.lesson: Rosh Chodesh is the head of the month: the blessings for the whole month flow from it, so behave especially well on that day.
